revisions.title: Unity and reach under pressure
revisions.body: Parmenides tests whether participation can preserve the Form’s unity and reach. If one Form is wholly present in many things, it would be separate from itself; if each receives a part, the Form is divided, and largeness, equality, and smallness yield absurdities. The likeness proposal generates a further Form, while separated domains block human and divine knowledge. This pressure ends in a demand for dialectical training before Socrates defines Forms.
